First listed 2026-09-09 · episode or wrap

Inside AI’s Fragile Ecosystem with Ed Zitron

Eisman and Ed Zitron examine concentrated AI financing, frontier-model economics, token spending and data-center delivery. Eisman explicitly shares concern about OpenAI and Anthropic counterparty risk and questions growth durability. Many financial assertions rely on private reports or estimates. Later primary filings support Anthropic growth deceleration and NVIDIA reciprocal financing relationships, while clarifying revenue definitions, operating results and the preliminary nature of financing platforms. Catastrophic outcomes remain scenarios rather than established forecasts.

Substack · 2026-09-09 ↗
Useful concentration-risk framework, but substantial unverified private-company arithmetic, causal inference and rhetorical overstatement. Anthropic subsequent filings complicate blanket claims of negative unit economics. Guest claims remain separately attributed.

How he reasons here

  • Trace the final cash payer through an investment supply chain.
  • Distinguish accounting profit, cash generation, committed financing and paid-in cash.
  • Separate API list prices from provider serving costs.
  • Stress concentrated counterparties and refinancing dependencies.
  • Treat a run-rate snapshot separately from recurring revenue and a forecast.
  • Check whether capex demand survives removal of the largest customers.
